clue.text: Smell servicemen in the river — what's up?

indicators.note: 'in' places the first pair of pieces inside the river named after it

parts.note: the Aire is a Yorkshire river, a crossword regular
BO is body odour
RN is the Royal Navy

explanation.surface: Some smelly soldiers wading in a river make someone ask what is going on.
explanation.walkthrough: BO for body odour is a crossword staple; the Aire is a river in Yorkshire, England.
explanation.definitionFit: Something flying overhead is literally up in the sky, so the question 'what's up?' is answered by a thing aloft.

clue.text: Study one in scarlet?

indicators.note: 'in' puts the single letter inside the colour word

parts.note: scarlet is a shade of red
one is A, the indefinite article

explanation.surface: Is a student who reads for a degree in scarlet robes a scholar?
explanation.definitionFit: To read a subject at university is the British way of saying you study it there.

clue.text: Under the well-watered valley? It's over this will transport people

indicators.note: 'over' asks for the whole thing to be flipped end to end, as when something is turned over

parts.note: sub- is the prefix meaning under
a ria is a river valley drowned by the sea

explanation.surface: A riddle about something below a flooded valley that carries people.
explanation.walkthrough: SUB and RIA make SUBRIA, which turned over gives the aircraft maker's name.
explanation.definitionFit: An Airbus is a large passenger jet, a machine built for carrying travellers between airports.

clue.text: Poor and ineffectual tennis player in America

indicators.note: 'in' sets the player's name inside the country's abbreviation

parts.note: US is the United States
Monica Seles, the champion tennis player

explanation.surface: A lament about a feeble tennis player competing in the United States.
explanation.definitionFit: Something weak and achieving nothing is of no worth at all, which is what this adjective describes.

clue.text: Means to travel quickly? It's hard

parts.note: a car is a means of travelling
apace means quickly

explanation.surface: A question about fast transport followed by the remark that it is difficult.
explanation.walkthrough: 'It's hard' reads as a comment on travelling fast, but it defines a hard shell.
explanation.definitionFit: A carapace is the rigid shell on the back of a tortoise or crab, a tough protective covering.

clue.text: They are taken in, notice — top group ('90s group) on the way up…

parts.note: an ad is a notice in a paper

indicators.note: in a down clue, going up means reading the letters from bottom to top

parts.note: set A is the top group in a streamed school class
Bros was a British boy band of the late 1980s and early 1990s

explanation.surface: A pop-music aside about bands, tied by an ellipsis to the next clue's song.
explanation.walkthrough: AD stays put; SET A plus BROS read upwards give SORBATES.
explanation.definitionFit: Adsorbates are the substances held on a surface by adsorption, so they are things taken in and retained.

clue.text: Golfer sent up by the Queen

definitions.note: an adjective meaning of a reign, glossed by a phrase

indicators.note: in a down clue, sending something up reads it from the bottom upwards

parts.note: Bernhard Langer, the German golfer

explanation.surface: A golfer being mocked by the monarch.
explanation.definitionFit: Regnal describes things relating to a monarch's reign, such as the regnal year counted from accession.

clue.text: Refinements as purveyed by "Cravats-R-Us"?

definitions.meaning: first meaning: fine details of etiquette
second meaning, split in two: pleasant neckwear, what a tie shop sells

explanation.surface: A joke about a necktie shop selling refinement.
explanation.walkthrough: Split the answer as NICE TIES and it is the stock of an imaginary cravat shop.
explanation.definitionFit: Niceties are small subtle points of manners or detail, the refinements of polite behaviour.

clue.text: A crowd in Germany surrounding new Russian fellow

indicators.note: 'surrounding' means the outer letters go round the next piece

parts.note: taken as written
N is the abbreviation for new
three's a crowd, and drei is German for three

explanation.surface: A German throng gathering around a newly arrived Russian man.
explanation.walkthrough: The saying 'two's company, three's a crowd' makes a crowd three, in German DREI.
explanation.definitionFit: Andrei is a common Russian male first name, the local form of Andrew.

clue.text: As a teacher, what you should have to get up? No

parts.note: the article taken as written; 'As' joins it
a BEd, Bachelor of Education, is a teaching degree

explanation.surface: Advice on what qualification a teacher needs, then a reluctant refusal to rise.
explanation.walkthrough: A BEd is what a would-be teacher should hold; 'to get up? No' describes staying put under the covers.
explanation.definitionFit: Someone still lying in bed has declined to rise, which is the old adverb for being in bed.

clue.text: When two women get together, it could be lethal!

wordplay.note: Bella and Donna are two women's names, also Italian for beautiful and lady

explanation.surface: A warning that a meeting of two women may end in death.
explanation.definitionFit: Belladonna is deadly nightshade, a plant whose berries are poisonous enough to kill.

clue.text: One gets up flowers

parts.note: I is the Roman numeral one
rises means gets up

explanation.surface: Someone getting out of bed, and some flowers.
explanation.definitionFit: Irises are garden plants with tall stems and showy blooms, often purple or yellow.

clue.text: Freight man in whose unconscious "vehicle" represents "energy"?

indicators.note: one thing representing another means it stands in its place, so one piece replaces another

parts.note: in Freud the superego is a largely unconscious part of the mind
a car is a vehicle
E is the symbol for energy

explanation.surface: A psychoanalytic riddle about a dreamer whose unconscious makes symbols.
explanation.walkthrough: In SUPEREGO, the E is replaced by CAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A supercargo is the officer aboard a merchant ship in charge of the cargo and its sale.

clue.text: What's testable in crash?

indicators.note: something in a crash gets smashed up, so the word is broken and rebuilt

parts.note: taken as written as anagram fodder

explanation.surface: What safety device can be put to the test in a car crash?
explanation.walkthrough: The whole clue defines the answer and the wordplay is the same words.
explanation.definitionFit: A seatbelt restrains a passenger in a collision, so a crash is the moment its strength is proved.

clue.text: A particular honour

definitions.meaning: first meaning: a detail or point

explanation.walkthrough: 'A particular honour' reads as one phrase, but splits into two meanings.
explanation.definitionFit: The noun means both a single point or detail and the esteem shown to someone admired.

clue.text: Jazz fan's about to catch some gossip

indicators.note: the fan is about, that is around, the next piece

parts.note: cat is old slang for a jazz enthusiast
to hitch is to catch or fasten

explanation.surface: A jazz lover about to pick up a bit of gossip.
explanation.definitionFit: Chitchat is light idle conversation, the small talk and tittle-tattle people swap.

clue.text: Secret police go about doctoring tapes

indicators.note: 'about' puts the outer word around the rearranged letters

parts.note: taken as written

indicators.note: doctoring is tampering with or altering, so the letters are rearranged

parts.note: anagram fodder taken as written

explanation.surface: Secret police tampering with recordings.
explanation.definitionFit: The Gestapo was the secret state police force of Nazi Germany.

clue.text: The "Thunderer" putting out an urgent entreaty for a large amount

indicators.note: the entreaty is put out, stretched around something placed inside it

parts.note: a plea is an urgent request
Thor is the Norse god of thunder

explanation.surface: The Times, nicknamed the Thunderer, publishing an appeal for a big sum.
explanation.walkthrough: The Thunderer is a nickname for The Times newspaper, but here it is the thunder god.
explanation.definitionFit: A plethora is an excess or great abundance of something, more than is needed.

clue.text: Indecent riches collected towards the middle

indicators.note: the letters are gathered up inside the neighbouring words

parts.note: found across the two words

explanation.surface: Ill-gotten wealth being gathered in toward the centre.
explanation.definitionFit: Centric means situated at or directed toward the centre point of something.

clue.text: Unsuccessful 1 is around — take it over

indicators.note: the cross-referenced word is around, enclosing the other pieces

parts.note: 1 down is AIRBORNE, and something airborne is above
R stands for recipe, Latin for take

indicators.note: 'over' asks for the short word to be turned the other way round

parts.note: taken as written

explanation.surface: A failed attempt at something, with an order to take charge.
explanation.walkthrough: R plus IT turned over gives RTI, which sits inside ABOVE. R for take is the prescription abbreviation.
explanation.definitionFit: An abortive attempt is one that fails to achieve its aim, coming to nothing.

clue.text: Show of disapproval? No, not half captivated by the sound of spring

indicators.note: something captivated is held captive, so it sits inside the next piece

parts.note: boing is the noise a spring makes

indicators.note: only half of the short word is kept

parts.note: the second half of the word

explanation.surface: Disapproval expressed, interrupted by the sound of springtime.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Spring' looks like the season, but it is the coiled metal that goes boing.
explanation.definitionFit: Booing is the jeering noise a crowd makes to show it dislikes a performer.

clue.text: Top means of transport divided the church

definitions.note: an adjective for a church, glossed by a phrase

parts.note: A1 is top quality, with 1 written as I
a sled is a sledge

explanation.surface: A fancy vehicle that split a congregation.
explanation.definitionFit: An aisled church has its nave split by rows of columns into a central space and side passages.

clue.text: (see 6 down)…with '80s/'90s song ã trouble in the past!

indicators.note: 'in' places the trouble inside the phrase for the past

parts.note: ago means in the past
ado is fuss or trouble

explanation.surface: Continuing the pop theme: a novelty song that caused trouble long ago.
explanation.walkthrough: Agadoo was a 1984 novelty hit by Black Lace, a British party band.
explanation.definitionFit: Agadoo is the title of a famous novelty pop single, a staple of discos and holiday parties.

clue.text: Winter race meeting: I'd the backing of Sea Province

parts.note: Nov, November, the month that opens winter in some reckonings
Ascot is the famous racecourse in Berkshire
I, with 'd (had) joining it to the next piece

indicators.note: the back of a word is its final letter

parts.note: the final letter of the word

explanation.surface: A winter horse-race meeting backed by a sea province.
explanation.walkthrough: Nov as winter is loose: November is a late-autumn month in Britain.
explanation.definitionFit: Nova Scotia is one of Canada's Atlantic provinces, a peninsula almost surrounded by sea.

clue.text: Commander and saint left horrified

indicators.note: the saint has left, gone away from the word that follows

parts.note: aghast means horrified
St is the abbreviation for saint

explanation.surface: A commander and a saint who departed in horror.
explanation.definitionFit: An agha is an Ottoman military officer or chief, a title for a commanding figure.

clue.text: Article about compiler giving the last word

indicators.note: the article goes about, enclosing, the next piece

parts.note: an is the indefinite article
the setter refers to themself as me

explanation.surface: A newspaper piece about the crossword setter that has the final say.
explanation.definitionFit: Amen is spoken at the close of a prayer or hymn, so it is literally the final utterance.

clue.text: "In" game with which to monkey puzzle

indicators.note: to monkey with something is to fiddle with it, so the letters are messed about

parts.note: taken as written
taken as written

explanation.surface: A trendy game in which to tease a monkey puzzle tree.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Monkey puzzle' looks like the tree; split, monkey is the anagram signal. Also the setter's own pseudonym, Enigmatist.
explanation.definitionFit: An enigma is a mystery or riddle, something baffling that must be worked out.

clue.text: The writer makes the effort to ring a few with similar measures

definitions.note: a noun for equality of measure, glossed by a plural phrase

parts.note: the writer is the setter, I
some means a few
a try is an effort

explanation.surface: The setter doing their best to phone a handful of people.
explanation.walkthrough: 'To ring' suggests putting one piece around another, but nothing is enclosed: the parts simply follow one another, and the surface's phoning is padding.
explanation.definitionFit: Isometry is equality of measurement, as in a mapping that preserves distances between points.
